questions: Is the edge reversal operation a global reversal of all edges in the graph, or does it only reverse edges incident to the current vertex?
Can the edge reversal operation be performed multiple times, and if so, does each reversal toggle the direction (so two reversals return to original orientation)?
Is the goal to minimize the total cost to reach vertex N, or is it to compute the cost of some specific sequence (like the first one that succeeds)?
Does moving along a directed edge require that the edge exists in the current graph state (after any reversals)?
If multiple edges exist from the current vertex, can we choose any, and does the choice affect the cost beyond the move cost of 1?
Is the graph allowed to have self-loops or multiple edges between the same pair of vertices?
Does the edge reversal operation reverse edges only among those that existed in the original graph, or does it also affect edges that were created by previous reversals?
Is the cost X incurred every time we reverse edges, regardless of whether the reversal changes reachable vertices from the current state?
